Recommended specimen and preparation: Conditioned board coupons; measure mass/area, thickness at multiple points and moisture using the selected validated method.
Allocation per treatment: 5 coupons per batch; 3 batches (15 per treatment).
Key record to retain: Parent sheet, conditioning, coupon area, instrument and calibration.

Test / endpoint: Coating add-on, dry thickness, coverage, pinholes, roughness
Recommended specimen and preparation: Coated coupons; determine gravimetric add-on and cross-sectional thickness at ≥5 positions; image surface coverage/pinholes.
Allocation per treatment: 5 coupons per batch; microscopy positions are subsamples, not independent specimens.
Key record to retain: Wet pickup, dry mass, coating area, section orientation, image scale and analysis settings.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Flat conditioned coupons; use fresh droplets at ≥5 locations per coupon and record time-dependent angle.
Allocation per treatment: 5 coupons per batch; ≥5 drops per coupon.
Key record to retain: Droplet volume, water quality, elapsed time, surface side and ambient conditions.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Separate coupons cut to the selected Cobb tester clamp area; do not reuse coupons after wetting.
Key record to retain: Exposed area, contact time, blotting procedure, pre/post mass and conditioning.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Independent barrier-test coupons sized to the instrument cell; seal edges and verify no leakage.
Key record to retain: Method, exposed area, temperature, RH on both sides, steady-state interval and blank/leak check.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Independent gas-transmission coupons sized to the instrument cell; condition at the same humidity used for comparison.
Key record to retain: Gas, temperature, RH, pressure, exposed area, conditioning and instrument range.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Separate uncreased coupons; apply the selected kit liquids in the prescribed sequence and record the highest passing level.
Key record to retain: Kit version, reagent set, exposure time, rating and failure location; analyse as ordinal.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Prepare separate strips in machine direction and cross direction to suit the tensile tester grips and selected standard.
Allocation per treatment: 5 MD + 5 CD strips per batch; 30 strips per treatment.
Key record to retain: Strip width/length, direction, gauge length, speed, conditioning and failure mode.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Separate uncreased coupons large enough for the selected burst tester clamp; avoid edge defects.
Key record to retain: Clamp area, diaphragm/tester calibration, pressure at rupture and specimen face.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Prepare separate tear-test pieces in MD and CD as required by the chosen method.
Allocation per treatment: 5 MD + 5 CD per batch; 30 per treatment.
Key record to retain: Specimen geometry, direction, initial cut, pendulum/range and rejected tests.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Use separate strips with consistent orientation and conditioning; do not use tensile or burst specimens.
Key record to retain: Fold tester settings, strip dimensions, direction, endpoint and censoring limit.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Separate strips; apply the defined wetting/immersion protocol immediately before testing.
Allocation per treatment: 5 MD + 5 CD per batch; 30 per treatment.
Key record to retain: Water temperature, soak time, blotting, time to test and dry-strength comparator.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Convert board from each batch into identical package geometry; control dimensions, score/crease and seam method.
Allocation per treatment: 5 packages per batch; 15 packages per treatment.
Key record to retain: Package dimensions, board orientation, seam, conditioning, loading rate and peak force.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Use independently packed units from controlled product lots. For repeated non-destructive observations, follow the same package IDs over days 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Use separate units for destructive tests.
Allocation per treatment: At least 6 packages per treatment per product lot; use separate additional units for destructive sampling and microbial tests.
Key record to retain: Product maturity/lot, fill mass, storage temperature/RH, headspace volume, package ID and rejection criteria.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Test finished coated article from each independent batch using simulants/conditions appropriate to intended food contact; include blank substrate and reagent controls.
Allocation per treatment: At least 3 independent finished-article specimens per batch and each relevant simulant/condition; laboratory to confirm regulatory sample mass/area.
Key record to retain: Overall/specific migration, heavy metals, pesticide residues, microbial limits, odour/sensory transfer and chain of custody.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Separate inoculated challenge units and uninoculated controls; select organisms and protocol with a qualified microbiology laboratory.
Allocation per treatment: At least 3 independent packages per treatment/control and time point; determine final n by power analysis and biosafety review.
Key record to retain: Organism/strain, inoculum, controls, recovery method, log CFU, detection limit and biosafety approval.

Recommended specimen and preparation: Record energy for each independently prepared coating batch; this is a batch-level process measurement, not a coupon test.
Allocation per treatment: One logged energy record per independent batch; 3 per treatment.
Key record to retain: Meter ID, calibration, start/end time, oven load, setpoint, actual temperature and mass dried.
